madam president, the european directive on the reinforcement of the presumption of innocence in criminal proceedings which we are discussing today is a step towards further safeguarding fundamental rights. it is particularly important to clarify that the presumption of innocence under that directive also includes any administrative side-effects of criminal prosecution, such as, for example, the automatic posting of an official on leave. it must be accepted that such provisions of national law are legitimate only where they are necessary measures having regard to the nature and the type of the criminal offence and provided that they are of a temporary nature and that their consequences are completely removed in the event of the defendant being acquitted in criminal proceedings. the exception to the presumption of innocence for administrative proceedings provided for in the sixth recital in the preamble to the directive concerns only the autonomous actions of the administrative authorities.

member of the commission.– madam president, the commission generally welcomes ms geringer de oedenberg’s report, which recognises the commission’s role in assisting the committee on petitions with cases raised by petitioners. in 2014, of the 790 admissible and followed—up petitions, 688 were forwarded to the commission. the commission shares the report’s opinion that there is a good working relationship between the committee on petitions and the commission. it welcomes the more careful screening that has been put in place by the committee on which institution or body is the best place to respond to a given petition. the commission does not, however, agree with the report’s observations that the commission imposed restrictions on procedural grounds to inhibit inquiries into the substance of petitions or suggested closing files without waiting for the outcome of the examination of the issues they raise. indeed, the commission would like to assure the honourable members that it responds to all the requests of the committee on petitions which fall within its competence and endeavours to assist the committee as best it can. no procedural restrictions have ever been imposed concerning the handling of petitions. however, there may well be cases where the commission cannot provide any detailed response to the committee as it has no competence in the matter. in such cases, the commission informs the committee of the matter accordingly. any decision to close a petition rests with the committee itself. the report calls on the commission to be represented in committee debates by an official with the highest possible rank. on this point, the commission would like to reassure the committee that it always sends its most competent officials for the issues concerned to the peti meetings, and has indeed not received any indications to date from peti members or from the peti secretariat that it was represented at an inappropriate level. regarding the report’s call for the transposition of eu law, the commission would like to recall that it actively remedies instances of incorrect transposition of eu law through the eu pilot and infringement procedures. as part of the better regulation agenda, the commission has reinforced its preventive action to support member states in the implementation process of union legislation. turning to the issue of making information on the developments in infringement proceedings directly linked to petitions available to the committee, i would like to clarify that such information is already available. the commission reports on its work in the annual report on monitoring the application of eu law, where it explains how it exercises its powers as guardian of the treaties, including a follow-up to petitions received from parliament. the commission also shares infringement-related information with parliament, in line with the current framework agreement, and discloses information on infringement procedures in the form of press releases, in particular at the stages of reasoned opinion and referral to the court. in addition, the decisions on infringement proceedings can be consulted on the commission’s searchable database available on europarl.eu. moreover, the commission is currently examining ways to improve the traceability of files on which petitions from parliament are sent to the commission. turning to the commission’s interpretation of article 51 of the charter of fundamental rights, it would like to recall that it is in line with the standing jurisprudence of the court of justice. regarding the report’s remarks on the european citizens’ initiative, the commission remains fully committed to assisting the european citizens’ initiative’s work, so that it reaches its full potential. the commission has already implemented – and will continue to implement – important measures to improve the functioning of the instrument under the current framework, in close cooperation with parliament, the member states and other eu bodies and stakeholders. the commission provided parliament with more detailed information in relation to these aspects in the plenary debate of 26 october 2015. the commission is considering further new actions to be implemented in several of the key areas highlighted in the parliament resolution on the european citizens’ initiative. however, as only three years have passed since the regulation’s effective entry into application, it is still too early to launch a legislative revision. the commission will, however, continue to work in 2016 to further assess the possible need for such a revision at a later stage. turning to the calls on the commission to implement the ombudsman’s recommendations and to take into account the peti committee opinion on the ttip negotiations, the commission is committed to maximising transparency wherever this can be done without undermining their core elements of confidentiality, considered essential for the negotiations. many of the ombudsman’s recommendations have already been implemented or are in the process of being implemented. the commission examined the citizens’ initiative on ttip in the context of article 11 of the treaty of european union, but it did not register it because the conditions laid down in regulation no 211 of 2011 were not met. the commission welcomes the report’s observations on the importance of the european year of citizens and it will continue to provide information and sustained participation in european democracy in the future, including by means of citizens’ dialogue in the member states. to this end, the commission consistently deploys the europe for citizens’ programme, in the application of which projects strengthening and facilitating the participation and involvement of european citizens in the european decision-making process are being funded. finally the commission thanks the committee for its support for solvit. the commission agrees that solvit should be further developed, and is currently working together with the member states to develop solvit to its full potential. in conclusion, i would like to reassure parliament of the commission’s continued and strong commitment to cooperating closely with it on petitions, which are a cornerstone of eu citizenship and a fundamental right under the treaty.

the rapporteur. mr president, today our parliament is exercising a leading function provided for by the treaty on the functioning of the european union, which is to exercise democratic control over the activities of the european central bank. the european central bank is not an independent european central bank. the european central bank is therefore accountable to the european parliament, the only eu institution directly elected by the people of the union. in previous years, the procedure for discussing the annual activity report of the european central bank in the european parliament's plenary session was limited to wish lists, with no criticism of the leadership of the european central bank and its actions. in this report we are putting our finger on the tip of the spear. although a special effort was made by certain political groups, within the committee on economic and monetary affairs, with joint compromise amendments, to remove important points of the report i had drawn up, although some tried to round off the corners, although the 'herakles of the crown' proved to be more 'strangely' than mr draghi, the key points of the report remain. the european central bank must take important steps to ensure that in the exercise of its mission there is no conflict of interest due to the fourfold action which has transformed the european central bank into a state within a state. and that's because the european central bank is supposed to be an independent monetary policy institution, while at the same time overseeing the 130 largest systemic banks in europe. at the same time, the european central bank is the big lender of the union countries, having bought bonds of the eurozone countries in the context of quantitative easing, and finally, it is a member of the troika which has bankrupted and impoverished the countries of the memorandum. the report therefore recalls the important and groundbreaking decision of the court of justice of the european union c-62/14, which sets out the terms and conditions under which the european central bank is obliged to implement the quantitative easing programme. a court decision that essentially calls for the european central bank to be expelled from the troika. at the same time, our report calls for transparency and control by the troika and, therefore, by the european central bank in the implementation of the so-called rescue programmes, i.e. the memoranda. mr draghi, unemployment remains extremely high, particularly among young people and the longterm unemployed, with rates varying widely, from 6.4% in germany to 26.6% in greece. and all this while the european central bank and the member states have spent several trillion euros on crisis response since 2009. at the same time, the ecb is particularly favourable to the continuation of the tough fiscal and austerity policies, which have not been able to reduce unemployment or public debt. the report even calls on member states to carry out an audit of the debt in accordance with the provisions of regulation (eu) no 472/2013. we also believe that a policy is needed to boost public and private investment and to stimulate growth. this requires increased liquidity and financing of smes. although the european central bank launched an ambitious quantitative easing programme that reached €582 billion at the end of 2015, of which €17 billion was spent by the central bank of impoverished greece, yet, mr draghi, neither deflation, unemployment, nor underdevelopment were adequately addressed. the report also stresses the need to ensure that the union's financial institutions are able to compete effectively with the world's financial institutions, and that the union's financial institutions are able to compete effectively with the world's financial institutions. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the report supports the european commission's proposed pan-european deposit guarantee scheme, but also points out the important steps taken towards the creation of a single supervisory authority for banks. the commission notes that the greek authorities have not provided any evidence that the bank of greece has been able to obtain a loan of eur [...] million from the bank of greece. therefore, there is a need for greater transparency in the way the ela is operated. in conclusion, mr president, i would like to thank the shadow rapporteurs for their positive contribution to this report.

vice-president of the commission.– mr president, first of all thank you for this debate. parliament has an important role in the debate on european economic policies, and it was positive to see such an engaged and informed debate. the commission fully supports the active role of the econ committee in the dialogue with the ecb, which is an important component of the ecb’s transparency and democratic accountability. the ecb has acted to address the risk of too prolonged a period of very low inflation, and it will continue to play a key role in the overall policy-setting of the euro area. it is now time for public authorities at all levels to take responsibility within their respective mandates. the impact of the crisis has not only been cyclical, it has also had a significant structural component and it has lowered the potential growth of eu economies. structural, fiscal and monetary policies each have a role to play in tackling this challenge. this year the commission will give a clear priority to initiatives which, if agreed quickly, can have a direct impact on jobs and growth. we will focus on new boosts for jobs, growth and investment. we will work to make the internal market deeper and fairer and strengthen its industrial base. finally, we will endeavour to make economic and monetary union deeper and fairer, building on the conclusions of the five presidents’ report.
president of the european central bank.– mr president, i am very thankful for this debate and i will try to respond to most remarks, though – i have to apologise in advance – not all of them, owing to time limits. by the way, some of the statements or questions were inherently political, and so the best equipped to answer are the national governments and the national parliaments, and perhaps your own parliament. let me just try to focus on the main points. i take from many of the questions that were asked that many of you have doubts about the effects of our monetary policy measures. let me try to explain why i have said several times that our policy measures are actually working. all the quantitative indicators show improvements in the provision of credit and financing conditions. to give you an idea, bank lending rates in the euro area have fallen by 80 basis points on average since mid-2014. we should also recall that the report you are addressing is 2014, but many things have happened since then. so let me give you an updated picture with respect to the report. the lending rates have fallen by 80 basis points since mid-2014 and by up to 140 points in the countries that were hit hardest by the crisis. second, these improved conditions have translated into higher credit and investment in the euro area, supporting economic growth and inflation and strengthening the resilience of the euro area in the face of adverse global developments. to give you an account of this, in may 2014, before the announcement of the credit-easing measures, the loans to the non-financial corporations, to firms and companies, contracted at an annual rate of 2.9%, but since july 2015 the contraction stopped and loans have started to grow. third, actions to ensure price stability bolster confidence in the euro economy as a whole and also support the ongoing recovery. we reckon that, if we had not taken our measures, the euro area would have been in outright deflation last year and prices would have fallen at an even quicker pace this year. to give an example, our staff has calculated that, in the absence of our credit measures and qe, growth would be one percentage point lower in the years 2015-2017. inflation would have been thoroughly negative in 2015, and certainly much lower than we are projecting now in 2016. when some of you – several of you – asked ‘what about the smes: how is all of this impacting the smes?’, well here i can repeat what i said in a press conference: that the pass-through of our measures into the real economy has been significant, if not spectacular, and the credit-easing package in june 2014 seems to have particularly benefited the smes, because the lending rates for small loans declined more than for large loans. regarding the recent surveys, there are two types of survey. one is the bank lending survey, where we ask banks what they plan to do and what are the major factors that they consider in deciding whether to give credit or not. the response is that, basically, there is no limiting factor today. then there is the commission’s survey – if i can quote it – and that says the last survey on smes’ access to finance reported an improvement in the availability of bank loans for smes and also in the willingness of banks to lend in the six months from april to september 2015. however, we have to acknowledge that lending rates for very small loans remain higher than for large loans, in particular in the vulnerable euro area countries, and that of course reflects the higher lending risk to smes to some extent. but certainly we want to overcome this situation. so there have been improvements. have the improvements been as much as we would like? not yet; we have to do more. we have to make sure that the smes’ credit conditions improve further. as far as monetary policy stands, i did say in my introductory statement that, in view of the increased downside risks to price stability, we stand ready – and the governing council stands ready – in accordance with our mandate to review, and possibly reconsider, our monetary policy stance in early march if warranted by incoming information. several of the questions and statements dealt with potential risks associated with low interest rates and our unconventional measures. these concerns relate, in particular, to a perception that low interest rates negatively impact on savers and that our policy may threaten financial stability, with respect especially to pension funds, insurance companies and savers in general. i have discussed these concerns on several occasions, but let me, however, stress the following. for savers, it is true that nominal rates on many types of savings in the euro area are currently very low by historical standards. i also explained that the low-interest-rate environment is actually a reflection of the current economic and structural conditions. so when i am asked how long this will last: it will last until the economic environment improves. so the low remuneration of savings is a symptom, rather than a cause, of the sluggish recovery after many years in which the economy has operated below its potential and unutilised resources have accumulated. imagine that we were to depart from the current accommodative monetary policy stance. what would happen? well, it is not difficult to imagine. we would further curtail economic dynamism and ultimately contribute to prolonging the period of low interest rates through further recession. but we should also note that deposits are not the only way in which savers invest their savings. so, if one takes a comprehensive view of the financial returns of a household, we see that other financial assets provide a buffer to counteract the low returns of bank deposits. let me quote a recent study by the bundesbank that showed that the real return on a typical german household portfolio since 2008 has been around 1.5%, which is certainly lower than the pre-crisis average – but it is certainly higher than many periods during the 1990s, for example. so i do not think we can talk about the expropriation of savings, as some have done – not today, but on other occasions. finally, the possible implications for savers have to be put in a broader context. savings are made out of incomes that must be earned. by supporting employment and encouraging investment in the context of continued sluggish demand conditions, our accommodative monetary policy therefore supports the capacity to save. concerns were also expressed on financial stability and how our monetary policy could have an impact on financial stability. of course, price stability – our objective – is the prerequisite and the basis for financial stability, and we have to stay focused on delivering price stability. at the same time, we are aware that monetary policy measures may have unintended side effects on the financial system, for instance, if low yields invite excessive risk-taking. but to address this we need macro- and micro-prudential measures as tools, not changes in our monetary policy stance. let me now just briefly mention comments made on the ecb’s involvement in the macro-economic adjustment programmes in general, which was another point that has been raised. when the troika was set up in early 2010, the european monetary union was not equipped to deal with member states losing market access. in the run-up to the first greek programme, member states saw an advisory role of the ecb alongside the commission and the imf, and it was considered to be a useful complement to assure a strong programme. in short, the troika was created to draw on the diverse experience of the institutions. there was not only a good reason to ask the ecb to provide its advice in the context of the programme work, but also a good case for the ecb to accept this request. successful programmes had to repair the transmission mechanism of monetary policy and to safeguard financial stability. let me stress that this set-up was codified in the esm treaty and by the co-legislators in the two-pack, and the court of justice confirmed its legality. in line with this, the ecb has since provided its advice in programmes in five member states. but we should not forget that the final responsibility for decisions on the programme design and financing lies with the eurogroup and with the eurogroup ministers in their capacity – and the esm – and not with the institutions involved in the programme. as i have said on other occasions, the ecb may not be part of the troika forever, but i believe the right timing for changing the current set-up needs to be carefully considered, and this is not for me to decide upon. a few remarks dealt with our transparency, and i can only say that this past year has been a year full of decisions that were meant to improve our transparency. certainly what we have done has strengthened our commitment. the publication of the account of our governing council meetings, and the calendars of my fellow executive board members and myself and the supervisory board chair, were two further major steps towards increased transparency. but our readiness to provide further information on topics of interest also underlines that the ecb is a transparent institution. to give you some examples: since september 2015, national central banks can publicly communicate about the provision of ela to the banks in their respective countries in cases where they deem such communication necessary. we also provided further information on our plans regarding the collection of granular credit and credit risk data, better known as anacredit. so i can assure you that the ecb monitors developments in the area of governance and access to documents with a view to further enhancing its transparency and therefore its accountability. let me now comment briefly on completing the european monetary union. as some of you have acknowledged, the five presidents’ report outlined a clear roadmap for moving ahead with euro area integration, and i certainly welcomed the commission’s proposals for short-term measures which should now be fully implemented. for the ecb, of course, the completion of the banking union is of the utmost importance. on the one hand, this means that commonly-agreed rules need to be implemented. the most prominent example of where further progress should be made is the transposition of the bank recovery and resolution directive (brrd) and the deposit guarantee scheme directive (dgsd) in all euro area member states. we are still missing a common backstop for the single resolution fund. we also need progress on the necessary, still-missing third pillar of the banking union, namely the common european deposit guarantee scheme. why is it important? because only such a system will ensure that depositors’ confidence is equally strong across countries and across the whole banking union, which is vital for the future of our economic and monetary union. implementing the short-term proposal of the five presidents’ report is important and may be necessary, but it is not a sufficient condition to completing the union. so i am looking forward to the proposals for developing the long-term issues. let me also recall, as i have done on other occasions, that for the euro area to prosper, the recovery cannot continue – and here i certainly agree with some of the statements today – to rely on monetary policy only. our monetary policy provides the room – as i said, it is an essential condition but is not in itself sufficient – for this recovery to become structural from what it is today, namely cyclical. there was one question about high-denomination banknotes. let me say that the executive board of the ecb has been considering this issue for some time now, and technical work is under way to look at high-denomination banknotes. we have not made a decision yet. there are questions on how to best implement a decision and how to communicate this. we want to make changes, but we want to make changes in an orderly fashion. but rest assured that we are determined not to make seigniorage a comfort for criminals.

the commission madam president, we are discussing the increase in endocrine disorders and diseases observed in recent years in a large part of the population. endocrine disruptors are chemicals that mimic hormones and interfere with the hormonal system, causing fertility disorders, tumours and various cancers. these substances are, as has been said, present in many products of everyday use and the individual consumer is unable to be aware of their existence, since these items often do not carry a declaration of content. it is therefore necessary for the european union to review existing relevant legislation and to have more requirements on chemicals contained in products such as food and beverages. in addition, changes should be made to the assessment, authorisation and restrictions of those substances in those products, and there should be greater transparency in determining whether a substance in this context has the properties to be prohibited.
the commission madam president, we are discussing transparency and control in the clinical trials process in the light of the recent tragic incident in france, where we had one dead and five people who are still in hospital and in danger. clinical trials are aimed at developing medicines and improving the therapies used, and within the european union, investment in clinical research exceeds eur 20 billion a year. however, there is often a lack of transparency and control in clinical trials. in addition, cases of concealment of any negative results in preliminary clinical trials and publication of only the desired results are also frequently observed. therefore, in order to ensure transparency in clinical trials, all pharmaceutical companies should declare and make public the results from the early stages of clinical trials, as also required by the world health organisation.

the commission madam president, mrs o'reilly's effort is commendable, considering the short time since she was elected. the role of the european ombudsman in helping the institutions of the european union to become more open, efficient and citizen-friendly, with a view to strengthening citizens' trust in the union, is very difficult. the idea of european integration must be accompanied by greater transparency and control of its institutions. the european parliament has already expressed its views on the commission's proposal for a regulation on the european union's external relations. in addition, there is a 20% of the ombudsman's proposals which the institutions have not complied with. there is still a long way to go in areas such as transparency, the rule of law, ethics, the fight against corruption in the management of conflicts of interest in the public sector, transparency in clinical trials and, above all, openness in the ttip negotiations. in this connection, i support the increase in the annual budget of the european ombudsman's office, but i would also like to see the legal binding of the ombudsman's suggestions considered.
the commission madam president, in many member states of the union, if not in all of them, the smuggling rates of tobacco products are much higher than those provided by the statistical services because of political and economic interests. the illegal tobacco trade has two aspects to consider: the interplay of politicians of all parties across europe, and the intrusive role of the big tobacco companies, who claim the lion's share of a large and profitable market. the interests are enormous and the budgetary implications at community and national level are immediate. the tobacco industry interacts at all levels of the decision-making process. for example, the four largest companies agreed to pay $2.15 billion to avoid legal penalties after lawsuits were filed. if they were innocent, they wouldn't pay such a huge amount. the commission's proposal is to be adopted by the council and the council, and the council is to be consulted on the proposal. in greece in particular, tobacco retailers are the big losers as the weak link in the market, while the losses to the public lead to increased unemployment, reduced insurance contributions and increased public health risk from smoking contraband cigarettes. the ratification of the world health organization's protocol on illicit tobacco and the implementation of independent tracing is a first step. we must also deal with the taxation of hookah tobacco, which has never been counted and for which there is no evidence of profits being lost, the refill liquids for e-cigarettes, which in some countries coincide with the excise duty, and the suppression of the markets of foreigners and illegal immigrants in which the illegality is impossible to control because of ghettos.
the commission madam president, as early as 2004, philip morris and the european commission signed a 12-year cooperation agreement to combat the illicit trade in cigarettes, to which the member states of the union have also acceded. however, the commission is postponing the publication of the evaluation of the agreement with philip morris. why is that ? why is the european parliament, the supremely democratic institution, not informed? what is the added value of this agreement? the european union and the member states must take serious measures to tackle cigarette smuggling, both for the protection of health and to combat tax evasion. at the same time, measures should be taken, particularly in greece, to support small-scale tobacco growers and retailers of tobacco products. we are waiting for your answers, madam vice-president, because this is a very serious matter, and you realize that all our colleagues have asked key questions.

the commission the commission has already taken a number of measures to combat the problem of malnutrition in greece. according to the prevention research institute, six out of ten greek students in 2013-2014 did not have access to adequate quality food. furthermore, for the 2014-2015 school year, 53% of students' families are food insecure and 21% are affected by hunger. this shows that european aid for the supply of fruit and vegetables and even dairy products to greek schools is half-baked and insufficient to tackle child malnutrition in greece, which has been facing a humanitarian crisis in recent years. it must be made clear to all sides that the eradication of malnutrition in schools cannot wait, as the health of children is at stake. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the budgetary authority is able to meet the requirements of the budget, and that the budgetary authority is able to meet the requirements of the budgetary authority.
the commission i would like to say that i am very pleased that the commission has taken the initiative of proposing a directive on the protection of the environment and the protection of the health of workers. i am very much aware that the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's food aid is not used to the detriment of the environment, and that the commission has also taken steps to ensure that the community's food aid is used to the detriment of the environment. i would of course like to point out that with the austerity policies being implemented by the european union this diet will perhaps be the only one that some greek children will have access to, since we have a huge increase in unemployment and many parents are unable to provide even the basic necessities for their children since they have zero income. at the same time, there is no welfare state to provide for them, as the limited resources available are now primarily directed towards meeting the needs of migrants.
the commission the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the animal health of the european union is not compromised by the fact that the european union is not a member of the european union. this is how we manage to control the quality of animal feed and also to detect, prevent and treat diseases which are transmitted to animals and then transmitted to consumers through the products they consume (meat, milk and cheese). the globalisation of trade and climate change pose serious risks to both animal and consumer health and the european union should therefore simplify and intensify checks on animals imported from outside the european union in order to ensure food safety and prevent the transmission of diseases to consumers. the need for this is illustrated by my own country, greece, which is frequently the target of smuggled sheep and goats, mainly from turkey but also from skopje, which have not undergone the required checks and therefore pose a health risk to both domestic breeds and consumers. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to finance the necessary measures.
the commission mr president, in order to ensure a high level of public health and food safety, measures to prevent and reduce the impact of animal diseases should be increased first. all member states of the union should therefore promote animal husbandry and welfare practices to reduce any threats to public health. in addition, the various types of surveillance carried out by animal health groups should be better used to ensure a more efficient use of resources. finally, there should be a simplified legislative framework in the european union for the protection of animal health, public health and animal welfare, and this means, among other things, reducing the use of antibiotics in livestock farming, using appropriate animal feed and controlling the import of animals, especially sheep, from turkey and skopje, where animal diseases are widespread and where there are no adequate animal health controls. in fact, sheep diseases from turkey have been transmitted to evros and other areas of greece, causing damage to greek farmers who have been impoverished by the memorandum and who should be compensated immediately and receive financial support from the european union.
i am speaking on behalf of the ppe group. the commission's proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling, presentation and advertising of foodstuffs intended for human consumption is a very good one. it is no coincidence that 75% of the european union's trade and 38% of intra-community trade is carried by sea, which indicates the importance of the sector. the regulation we are about to vote on in the house is therefore designed to boost the efficiency of european ports and improve the overall quality of port services with a view to modernising them. it also creates conditions for fairer competition, reduces legal uncertainty, enhances transparency and improves the allocation of public resources. only the creation of a stable legal environment governed by fair conditions of competition and specific rules of transparency can attract investment in ports, contributing to the development of the european union economy, especially in times of economic crisis. the new legislation also gives ports greater autonomy in setting port charges. this increases competition both between european ports and between ports of the european union and third countries. in addition, it provides for a number of provisions favourable to small ports in order to avoid disproportionate administrative burden and additional fees and costs. europe needs such legislative initiatives that highlight the common interests between member states and stimulate the single internal market. in writing. ‒ the this report aims to highlight the extremely vulnerable position of refugee and asylum seeker girls and women, given the various forms of gender-based persecution that a large number of them face in their countries of origin and their already fraught situation in their attempt to reach europe. the aim is to avoid secondary victimisation of these people during the asylum process, even in countries considered safe. it is therefore imperative to ensure a gender-sensitive asylum policy that looks forward to the material and psychological support of these people. in particular, it is proposed to differentiate between men and women at the asylum application and distribution stages in reception centres, to provide staff with mandatory training on sexual and psychological violence and to promote them on the labour market. i therefore voted in favour of the report.

the commission shall adopt the following measures: ‒ the the general objective of the agreement is to ensure a high level of protection of personal data in the fields of police and judicial cooperation in criminal matters for the purpose of preventing, investigating, detecting or prosecuting criminal offences. it is, however, contrary to the general principles of the protection of personal data. the act demonstrates that commitments in the areas of intelligence sharing are subject either to personal will or to national security credentials, with the recent example of the paris and brussels terrorists, where the intelligence services of member states did not exchange information. the agreement does not effectively enhance the risk-based approach, nor does it ensure its obligation, by design and by default, to protect data. moreover, the provision of harmonised criteria, conditions and limitations is contrary to the provision in the agreement to include private entities in the concept of 'competent authorities'. in conclusion, cooperation is practically impossible, given the simple example of the german authorities' failure to extradite christophorus to greece for investigation into the siemens scandal. for all these reasons, i vote against.
ecr), in writing. ‒ i support the recommendation for second reading on the council's position at first reading with a view to adopting a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data and repealing directive 95/46/ec, because it is complete and well-founded.
the commission shall adopt the following measures: ‒ the the package of legislation voted in the european parliament under the false title of 'protection of personal data' legitimises the generalized package of everything under the banner of eu legislation. it provides for an exception to any protection if it is 'necessary and proportionate in a democratic society to prevent the impeding of investigations, to prevent and detect criminal offences, to protect public policy, national security or the rights of third parties'. the exceptions are of such a scope and generality that they essentially reduce the case to a rule. it also allows the collection and exchange of data relating to all political and social action. the rules are that data is transferred and exchanged between the various intelligence and security services, not only of the eu member states but also of third countries and imperialist organisations (usa, nato, etc.). anyone can be targeted by the repressive mechanisms without being suspected of any act, simply for reasons of public order and security! the monopolies and their associations see in the rights and freedoms of the people a danger to their power. that is why their defence is inseparable from the struggle to overthrow them, to bring about radical changes in power and the economy.
the commission shall adopt the following measures: ‒ the the proposed regulation replaces directive 95/46/ec, so it has more legal weight, but it basically fills the gaps in the protection of personal data that the directive had. specific and characteristic: 1. the accountability of controllers and processors is strengthened, and penalties are introduced to incentivise controllers to comply with the regulations. 2.codes of conduct and legally binding certification mechanisms are introduced, such as the right to 'write off' (a person who no longer wishes his data to be processed, they are deleted), but also to facilitate users' access to their data. 3. provide enhanced and enforceable rights for citizens, and also provide for prohibitions on the processing of personal data concerning children. 4. most importantly, the independence of supervisory authorities is strengthened so that each national authority can work without interference, as was not the case with the personal data breaches of golden dawn officials during the political persecutions.

gue/ngl), in writing. ‒ the the vote on the proposal for a european parliament and council directive on the use of passenger name record (pnr) data for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences concerns a particularly sensitive area which we are called upon to manage. i think it is a very wrong approach to propose that the only solution is to collect data on all types of movement, whether personal or non-personal, without any further adequate safeguards, especially when we all know that the continuous production of data cannot be managed effectively or produce the desired results. in this context, the report does not contain the elements which would lay the foundations for a functional and effective response to the risks that exist and that is why i voted against it.
the commission shall adopt the following measures: ‒ the air carriers and non-carrier economic operators already collect and process pnr data, so the directive does not introduce anything new, because criminals and terrorists are not used to using air transport for their travels. the main point is that the obligation to apply a system for the collection of personal data in crossborder road and/or sea transport is not considered, since this would mean the automatic abolition of the schengen acquis, nor does it make it compulsory for member states to exchange data when there is tangible evidence of the existence of persons involved in international crime. in addition, it is important that the results of the processing of pnr data should not be used to deny asylum to suspected or identified criminals or terrorists. the directive leaves gaps in the privacy rights of union citizens and is not in line with the data retention directive. finally, in the sense of a sovereign state, each member state should be able to exclude those minor offences for which, taking into account its respective criminal justice system, the processing of pnr data would not be in accordance with the fundamental principle of proportionality of the tfeu. i voted against all of these.
in writing. ‒ the present report deals with the proposal for a directive that attempts to regulate the use of passenger name record (pnr) data at eu level and to harmonise member states’ policies in this field. i strongly believe it is crucial not to adopt an amplified approach of an eu pnr system that could alienate fundamental rights under the pretext of the recent terrorist attacks. deplorably, as it stands from the report, the pnr proposal does not meet the criteria of proportionality, mostly due to the fact that the personal data can be assessed in a non-targeted way. additionally, the enlargement of the scope of the eu pnr scheme beyond international targeted flights in order to include intra-eu flights will finally lead to the collection of data of everyone flying between eu member states. this fact raises an issue of compliance with the principle of necessity. therefore, i voted against.
ecr), in writing. ‒ i am voting against the second report on the proposal for a directive of the european parliament and of the council on the use of passenger name record (pnr) data for the prevention, detection, investigation and prosecution of terrorist offences and other serious criminal offences, for the reasons i set out in detail in my speech to the european parliament's plenary session in strasbourg on 13 april 2016, and because the report is not complete and well-documented.
the commission shall adopt the following measures: ‒ the the new pnr system, i.e. the records of passengers of air flights within and outside the eu, is enlarging the network of repression of the eu and of the civil governments at the expense of the people. passenger data comprising 19 categories of data will be retained and exchanged by the intelligence services of member states and third countries for at least 5 years. on this basis, passengers will be categorised according to the number and type of trips they make, their frequency, intermediate stations, days spent, financial data, etc. the ground is also being prepared for the subsequent extension of the passenger file system to all modes of transport. the claim by the political representatives of the monopolies that passengers' personal data are protected because after 30 days they will be 'anonymised' and a 'data protection officer' will be appointed is not convincing. the aim of all these repressive mechanisms is to restrict people's freedoms and rights which the monopolies, the eu and governments see as a threat to their power. that is why the popular struggle for their defence and expansion is inextricably linked to the overthrow of the power of capital and the liberation from the shackles of its associations.
the commission shall adopt the following measures: ‒ the air carriers and non-carrier economic operators already collect and process pnr data, so the directive does not introduce anything new, in the sense that criminals and terrorists are not used to using air transport for their travels. in particular, however, it does not consider the obligation to apply a system for the collection of personal data in crossborder road and/or maritime transport, as this would mean the automatic abolition of the schengen acquis, nor does it make the exchange of data between member states mandatory where there is tangible evidence of the existence of individuals involved in international crime. in addition, it is important to ensure that the results of the processing of pnr data cannot be used to deny asylum to suspected or identified criminals or terrorists. the directive leaves gaps in the right to privacy of union citizens and is not in line with the data retention directive. finally, in the sense of a sovereign state, each member state should be able to exclude those minor offences for which, taking into account its respective criminal justice system, the processing of pnr data would not be in accordance with the fundamental principle of proportionality of the tfeu.

s&d), in writing. ‒ the this report examines the establishment of a regulatory framework for indices used as benchmarks in financial instruments and financial contracts and form the basis of some retail services such as mortgages and loans. the text reached after the tripartite dialogue ensures the existence of a framework aimed at ensuring the principle of proportionality by imposing different conditions for each of the three categories of evaluation criteria: decisive, significant and non-significant. i personally voted in favour of this report, supporting the text which emerged from the trialogue.
the commission shall adopt the following measures: ‒ the the pricing of many financial instruments and contracts depends on the accuracy and integrity of benchmarks, which are subject to conflicts of interest and to systems of discretion and poor governance, which are vulnerable to counterfeiting. the third example is deutsche bank, which was fined for manipulating the libor benchmark, thus illegally earning hundreds of billions of euros at the expense of borrowers. these indicators undermine market confidence and as a result cause losses to consumers and investors. they contribute to the fragmentation of the internal market, have a serious impact on financial stability and the real economy, strangle national economies, act, under the cover of union law, as a lever for the pressure and constraint on national banking institutions and do not fully ensure the integrity and transparency of the market or economic reality, and cannot act as potential destabilising factors for the internal market and national financial activities. i therefore vote against this report.

gue/ngl), in writing. ‒ the i voted in favour of the report which contains the evaluation of the report of the european investment bank (eib) for the year 2014. the rapporteur presents the main theoretical objectives set by the eib, such as prioritising investment to accelerate recovery, promoting youth employment, innovation and smes, and economic and social cohesion and convergence, etc. however, it also points out that there are significant problems arising from the use, in many cases, of eib financing to support economically unsustainable infrastructure projects, in relation to public interest and environmental measures. the eib is therefore invited to make a number of interesting recommendations, in particular to update its activities and support investment needs in urban, health, education and social infrastructure, as well as the need for closer cooperation between the eib, national development institutions and the eu.

ecr), in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of the report on public access to documents for 2014 and 2015 for the reasons i set out in detail in my speech to the european parliament's plenary session in brussels on 27 april 2016 and because the report is complete and well-founded.
the commission shall adopt the following measures: ‒ the the report on public access to documents is characterized by the well-known exorbitant emphasis on the public's right to information, while it is deliberately characterized by a number of vague exceptions which ultimately cancel out any access to documents. the proposals for 'appointment of a commissioner responsible for the subject' or 'publication of documents relating to the legislative procedure' are perverse. they conceal that as long as the monopolies, eu and governments are in power, either by "secret" or "open" documents, they will legislate in the interests of the bourgeoisie, while the people will suffer from anti-people politics. the provision for a 'mandatory register of special interest groups' which effectively legalises the well-known 'lobbies'. in the name of transparency, this facilitates the unhindered involvement of business interests in the decisions taken, including those of the european parliament. the demands for 'combating leakage' are backed up by the attempts of monopolies to dominate at the expense of other competitors. the report concludes by stating that it expects 'more active participation of citizens in the decision-making process', but the truth is that only when workers take the keys of the economy into their own hands, conquer political power, will they decide for themselves their future.

the commission madam president, according to the european union, the application of international accounting standards enables companies to attract capital and investment on the international capital markets, thus helping to strengthen the single market. of course, the financial crisis has shown that these standards need to be reviewed. in particular, international financial reporting standards should enhance accountability and reduce the investor-to-business gap in order to protect investments. this will also enhance international comparability and hence transparency in the presentation of the real situation of economic units. moreover, as regards the application of international accounting standards in a member state, there should be harmonisation of the institutional and legal environment and better information of auditors and accountants on the technical details of their application. finally, transparency and credibility in the competent supervisory and regulatory authorities should be enhanced.

in writing. the commission proposal and the european parliament report reflect the sharpening of the contradictions between the imperialist centres and sections of capital, the need for the eu to take measures to protect its internal market and its monopoly groups. it is not aimed at, nor is it sufficient for, a tax relief for the lower classes. in a world of free movement of capital, multiple laws to legally avoid taxation by businesses and special tax regimes, the tax burden falls on the shoulders of the working people. it is no coincidence that in the eu-28 corporate taxation represents only 2.5% of gdp out of 40% of total taxation. the cpe was placed in white because the proposed arrangements do not change the specific correlation, they serve the same class orientation of eu tax policy. it is not by chance that measures which could lead to a shift of the tax burden to large capital are excluded, such as full denomination of shares, effective abolition of commercial and other secrets, taxation of all distributed and non-profit corporations, taxation of the current value of shares and changes in this value. the aim of eu policy and of this directive is to regulate competition between competing economic interests of different parts of the capital.

the commission mr president, we are discussing the transfer to the general court of the european union of jurisdiction to hear at first instance disputes between the union and its officials. it was originally proposed by the court of justice and the general court that the number of judges of the general court be increased to 56 so that each member state could appoint two judges. the increase also required the abolition of the civil service tribunal. however, the present regulation decides to increase the number of judges of the general court from 40 to 47 and to abolish the civil service tribunal, which consisted of 7 judges, who will be transferred to the general court. finally, given that there has been a 65% increase in cases brought before the general court between 2000 and 2010 compared to 1300 cases pending at the end of 2010, it is necessary to increase the number of judges to 56, two per member state, in order to cope with the increased workload of the general court.

the commission the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment against the adverse effects of certain substances and preparations is a very good one. however, union legislation, while respecting the principles of proportionality and subsidiarity, cannot be uniform for all member states. the development of each country must be taken into account, as must its historical contribution to emissions. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the european parliament is able to exercise its right to vote and to stand as a candidate in the elections to the european parliament. the principle of historical contribution to greenhouse gas emissions should therefore also govern community legislation on emission limits for non-road mobile machinery. in addition, the economic realities of each country and particularly the production sector must be taken very seriously. we cannot ask for greek farmers to adapt to the new emission limits for agricultural machinery on the one hand, and on the other hand, at the same time, be subject to a violent tax policy because of the memoranda.

the commission mr president, the importance of forests on a global scale is great, not only because they help to reduce greenhouse gases, and especially carbon dioxide, thus limiting climate change, but also because they are an important source of wealth for the countries that have them. the protection of forests against illegal logging and deforestation must therefore be treated by the european union as a matter of the highest priority. the european union must develop a policy in this area and cooperate not only with the member states of the union but also with those countries which produce large quantities of timber in order to curb illegal logging and trade in goods whose production involves deforestation. the commission must also provide adequate funding for this effort and conclude the necessary trade agreements to ensure that the programme can be successful. finally, the issue of limiting both illegal logging and forest destruction caused either by fires, arson or by accidental events must also be addressed within the framework of the european union.
the commission mr president, illegal logging and deforestation have serious environmental impacts, reducing biodiversity and contributing to climate change. to address environmental damage caused by illegal logging and deforestation, the european union has since 2003 adopted an action plan on forest law enforcement, governance and trade, aimed at encouraging sustainable forest management. this action plan has not yet produced the desired results. according to the court of auditors of the european union, the €300 million distributed to 35 countries under the scheme has had a meagre impact. the commission should therefore take immediate action to combat illegal logging and deforestation. at the same time, mr vella, the union should give financial aid to greece to repair the damage suffered by producers and their plant and animal capital as a result of the recent fires in chios, euboea and corfu. the same must of course apply to cyprus, which also suffered from fires this year.

i am speaking on behalf of the ppe group. mr president, i should like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr de jong, and the other rapporteurs. as the commissioner, mrs jurova, has said, we are moving into the area of criminal law and we are talking about the rights of suspects and accused persons, because of the need, thanks to this agreement which has already been secured, to adopt a directive which will substantially harmonise the laws of the individual member states. we all know that the right to legal protection of the suspect and the accused in a difficult situation and facing the possibility of deprivation of liberty must be guaranteed in practice and not just in theory. the commissioner has rightly pointed out that the quality of legal protection and legal aid that a suspect or an accused person can expect in practice often depends on his financial capabilities. the member state's response to this problem must be to guarantee the right of these persons to financial cover from special funds. the provisions of law ensuring the protection of such persons should also be harmonised by the member states. we are aware, of course, that these rights, such as the presumption of innocence, are guaranteed not only by the constitutions of the member states but also by national law based on international instruments such as the echr. we also see in the member states too many cases of suspects or accused persons who, both in preliminary and in the main proceedings, refer to the european court of justice, invoking article 6 of the echr, and accuse the member state in which they are, whether they are nationals of the member state or foreigners, of inaction in respect of the promotion and protection of their individual rights, and in particular of the rights guaranteed by the constitutions and by legislation of supranational importance. ladies and gentlemen, i know from my thirty years of experience as a lawyer, and in criminal law, that the member states have legal rules that protect and defend the rights of suspects and accused persons. but what we are seeking today and will be voting on tomorrow is the harmonization of the laws, so as to preserve the european construction from the divergences between the member states in relation to the different levels of protection they provide. the fact that all citizens of the european union can expect the same protection of their rights is ultimately in the interests of the rule of law and justice.
the commission is therefore proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the following areas: mr president, today's debate is about strengthening the rights of citizens and the proper functioning of justice at european level. the right to be represented by a lawyer is one of the most fundamental aspects of the right to a fair trial, as enshrined in both the charter of fundamental rights of the european union and the european convention on human rights. in particular, in the light of the ongoing economic and social crisis affecting millions of european citizens, we must ensure that accused or suspected persons are able to be effectively represented before the authorities. the timely provision of legal assistance and the extension of its scope to any member state where evidence is being taken or other investigative measures are being carried out are imperative steps. at the same time, the obligation on member states to ensure the quality and independence of the legal aid provided, combined with the existence of legal remedies for infringements of this right, will contribute to safeguarding citizens' rights. i therefore believe that today's procedure can help to improve the position of european citizens and at the same time create a positive climate for intensifying cooperation between member states.
the commission proposes a text based on the principle of mutual recognition of judicial decisions and the road map for strengthening the economic rights of suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. however, ensuring a minimum level of legal aid in all member states should not be limited to only two categories, namely suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings who are deprived of their liberty and wanted persons subject to proceedings relating to the execution of a european arrest warrant. such a piecemeal approach neither enhances legal certainty nor clarifies the degree and quality of entitlement to legal aid. it is true that there are differences between member states as regards the quality and remuneration of legal aid provided. we believe that a horizontal legislation on legal aid and representation will only exacerbate the problems that already exist and will not lead to a solution.
mr president, the european commission has since 2013 adopted the proposal for a directive on temporary legal assistance for suspects or accused persons and on legal assistance in european arrest warrant proceedings, in accordance with article 6 of the echr, i.e. the european convention on human rights. this means that suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings should have the right of access to a lawyer, whether or not they are deprived of their liberty. the member states are thus obliged to provide adequate legal aid to persons who lack the necessary resources and who are suspected or accused of a criminal offence. in addition, each country of the union must provide legal aid to suspects or accused persons without undue delay and require the presence of a defence lawyer before any procedural action. finally, the right to legal aid must be based on control of the resources of the applicant and each member state must take measures to improve the quality of legal aid itself for suspects or accused persons in order to comply with the echr's imperative to ensure a fair trial.

madam president, the death penalty, torture and all forms of cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment and punishment are prohibited by international and european treaties. in this context, the european regulation against torture must function effectively as a tool to protect people from violent treatment by imposing effective controls on items and activities used for capital punishment or torture. this objective requires an immediate reorganization of the european commission's controls on the trade in instruments of torture, a reorganization which, unfortunately, has been delayed on several levels. the advertising and sale of these products on the internet should therefore be prohibited. in particular, controls on exports of dual-use items included in the military equipment lists, which can also be used for torture, should be strengthened. i therefore believe that the european union cannot demand the ratification of international conventions against the death penalty in third countries and at the same time tolerate the use by the security forces here in the european union of practices and tools which are proven to result in permanent injury or even death.

the commission madam president, after the implementation of the schengen treaty and on the basis of the union's founding act as the european economic community, crossborder trade still faces the distortions of a complex mechanism of customs legislation. twenty-eight different member states apply as much severity as they can and impose different sanctions. but this has a direct impact on cross-border trade, resulting in a loss of revenue for member states. this is particularly true in countries where products originating in non-eu countries are imported and then transported across borders to the rest of europe. the union failed the examinations on the major issues: the economy, cross-border trade, illegal immigration, the fight against terrorism. member states, with nationalist governments that safeguard their national borders free from bigotry and enclosures, will be able to cooperate to increase the efficiency of customs controls on goods and to curb revenue evasion.

the commission madam president, there is no doubt that the agreement between the european union and iran on the country's nuclear programme is a major success of the european union's foreign policy and has opened up the field of cooperation between the two sides in various fields. iran is the second largest economy in the middle east and a major player in the energy trade, because it is the second largest country in the world in natural gas reserves and the fourth largest in oil. the european union's cooperation with iran in various fields, such as trade, industry and energy, is therefore in the interest of the countries of the european union, so that they are not dependent on one supplier in the energy sector. the european union has finally decided to differentiate its foreign policy from that of the united states. so after the nuclear deal, he lifted sanctions against iran, which the united states did not do, and as a result, combined with the fact that trade with iran is in dollars, there is a problem with the european union's trade with iran, which must be in euros. finally, iran can be an important stabilizing factor in the middle east, but it must also improve human rights and abolish the death penalty for young people under the age of 18, especially children.

the commission madam president, the union's mechanism for democracy, the rule of law and fundamental rights is invalid and illegal because, on the one hand, it is provided for in article 7 of the treaty, and on the other hand, it violates the principle of interinstitutional agreements. it is another attempt by professional manipulators to manipulate the national policies of the member states. it is unacceptable and undemocratic to give a new authority the power to monitor member states, and it is a waste of resources, since there are already international bodies monitoring violations of fundamental rights. commissioners jourová and timmermans have repeatedly stated that there are no violations of fundamental rights. nevertheless, there is a continuing attempt at political domination over the member states, just as in the case of greece with the implementation of bailout memoranda or in the cases of poland and hungary with legitimate constitutional amendments and referendums respectively. remember that, according to article 4 of the treaty, the union is obliged to respect the national identity of the member states, which is inherent in their fundamental political and constitutional structure, including regional and local selfgovernment.

the commission madam president, plant health is a key factor for sustainable and competitive agriculture, forestry and, more generally, for the biodiversity of the member states of the union. the current union regulatory framework on plant health aims to prevent the introduction and spread of harmful organisms that can destroy european agriculture and forestry. but so far we have not seen the desired results of this policy. the high volume of plant species imports from other continents implies a high potential for the establishment of pest outbreaks, while climate change allows those organisms to survive in europe and makes crops and ecosystems more vulnerable to new pests. the classic example is xylella, which destroyed thousands of olive trees in greece and italy. it is therefore necessary for the union to take measures to ensure that specific restrictions and requirements are respected when plant products are imported and moved.
the commission madam president, plant health is an important factor in the conservation of forests, shrubland and public and private green spaces, and contributes both to the development of agriculture and to the preservation of jobs associated with these activities. we must protect our producers from the introduction, especially from other continents, of pests which affect european trees which are not so resistant to them. so if trees are destroyed, agriculture, forestry, horticulture will be destroyed. the european union must therefore take the necessary measures to ensure that this phenomenon is both legally covered and dealt with in practice. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
the commission madam president, the food industry is now increasingly using trans fatty acids as they are a cheap ingredient in the production process and their use guarantees long life in the products. however, high consumption of trans fatty acids has been associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular disease and is a risk factor for developing coronary heart disease, which is responsible for approximately six hundred and sixty thousand deaths per year in the european union. at the same time, in the member states of the union, most of the population lacks adequate information on trans fats and their health effects, while at the same time, action by european countries to reduce the consumption of trans fats is limited. it is therefore necessary for the european union to propose mandatory limit values for trans fatty acids in order to improve the health of the citizens of the european union.

in writing. violence against women and gender-based violence are unfortunately still widespread in the european union. recent studies show that one third of all women in europe have experienced physical or sexual violence at least once in their adult lives, while around 20% of young women have been sexually harassed online. the fight against and elimination of all forms of violence against women, the right to equal treatment and non-discrimination are fundamental rights enshrined in the european treaties. what remains is to root these rights deeply in the foundations of our societies and to put them into practice and everyday life, changing anachronistic attitudes and perceptions. the istanbul convention is an important legal text that covers the issue of violence against women at various levels, setting out specific commitments and objectives, such as prevention, combating discrimination, criminal sanctions to address impunity, and protection and support for victims. the eu's accession to the convention will ensure a coherent european legislative framework to prevent and combat violence, but above all it will set an example for ratification of the convention by all european member states.

the commission mr president, value added tax (vat) is an important source of revenue for each member state and at the same time makes a significant contribution to the increase in revenue of the european union. this is why the european union is advocating the creation of a common vat system, under the pretext that goods and services will be taxed in the country where they are supplied. that sounds like a good idea. the tax system in each country is different, however, and it is on this that the development of the country's economy depends. the leveling of everyone into a common vat tax system will therefore create economic disruption and loss of revenue. the real purpose of this proposal is to deprive the states of the ability to manage their own economies and to satisfy their own needs and aspirations, and to cede this right to the european union. the consequences of this policy have been seen in greece, where the troika has destroyed the country's economy and has imposed a 24% value added tax on the final consumer... the rapporteur. madam president, the report on the responsibility for offshore oil and gas activities is the result of a long effort to bring about changes for the benefit of europe and its citizens. the proposals in this report do not only affect economic activities but are also intended to support the environmental needs of the european periphery. operations related to oil and gas production have a significant economic impact and a high environmental risk. most of the oil and gas activities take place either in the north sea or in the mediterranean. the nature of this work makes it extremely important to ensure the protection of businesses, which are directly linked to the environment. the commercial fisheries sector and the people involved in the fish farming sector can suffer significant economic losses from accidents or misuse of chemicals. the commission notes that the airport services agreement concluded between the airlines and the airlines was signed on 30 june 2012 and entered into force on 1 january 2013. it is therefore obvious that we must have rules to protect all those economic activities which are located close to offshore activities, exploitation of oil and gas fields, given that over 90% of the oil and 60% of the gas produced in europe comes from such offshore activities. it is also of the utmost importance that there are mechanisms for compensating for damage caused by offshore activities and corresponding mechanisms aimed at restoring ecosystems. the current european directive makes the holders of offshore licences responsible for preventing and remedying any environmental damage resulting from their activities. it also requires member states to establish procedures for dealing with compensation claims. however, the directive does not deal with liability for damage to natural or legal persons in respect of injury or pecuniary damage, nor with criminal liability for offshore accidents. the importance of further harmonised rules and of a compensation mechanism for offshore accidents should therefore be assessed in order to facilitate access to justice for victims. to promote this harmonisation, the possibility of establishing a fund based on fees paid by offshore industries could also be considered. we also need a european union action plan to prevent and combat the consequences of oil and gas accidents. their impact has serious and long-term implications for the marine environment and this should be taken into account in the directive. the commission should cooperate with the member states in order to speed up the relevant procedures. risk analysis and environmental impact assessment for offshore activities could also be published on a regular basis, according to parameters such as biodiversity, climate change, sustainable land use, protection of the marine environment and appropriate staff training before any authorisation of operations. it is my personal belief that prevention is better than cure and that the institution of criminal liability at european level could be an additional deterrent, in addition to existing civil penalties, thus leading to better protection of the environment and citizens.
the commission madam president, oil and gas make up half of the european union's energy mix and will continue to be the main sources of energy for several years to come. at the same time, an increasing proportion of these sources are coming from offshore activities. it is therefore of the utmost importance to ensure a high level of safety and to prevent natural disasters from these offshore activities. the deepwater horizon accident in the gulf of mexico cost billions of dollars to the american economy. we therefore understand that a similar accident in a closed sea such as the mediterranean would be many times more devastating, and that is why stricter rules and standards should be established on the liability of oil companies, and because these disasters do not stop at the borders of states, this high level of safety in offshore oil activities should apply everywhere. in particular, in view of the work in the ionian and adriatic, albania should comply with these rules and finally stop claiming the greek eez.
