the commission the european union must not be allowed to become a mere spectator, but must be able to take part in the process of european integration, and this must be done in a spirit of solidarity and solidarity. but it is not humanistic to cram refugees into makeshift camps and then serve the social dumping imposed by multinationals. the european union must respond decisively to the flows of refugees and migrants. the european union must therefore step up its efforts to bring peace to the middle east, crack down on the traffickers' networks and put pressure on erdogan to implement the eu-turkey agreement. the valletta agreement must also be implemented, the relocation of refugees from greece and italy to other countries of the union must be completed and the ineffective and unfair dublin iii rules must be urgently changed. the greek people must not pay for the european union's confrontations and short-sighted policy. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the situation in the islands is not worsened. greece is not a storehouse of souls.
the commission i would like to ask you, mr president, ladies and gentlemen, a question: in the morning, when you leave your home, you probably lock your door. the same is true at night, before you go to sleep. why would you do that? are you afraid of a stranger coming in? are you xenophobic, racist and intolerant? just as you have the right to protect your home and to choose whom you will receive and host, so do countries. it's not a matter of xenophobia, it's a matter of legality. you are very willing to baptize those who do not agree with the prevailing liberal ideology as extremists and extremists, while you demonstrate daily by your practices your concept of a democracy, where everyone is free to say whatever they want, as long as they do not disagree with your views. i would also like to say that i have never seen you concerned about the systematic racism and discrimination against the indigenous people of europe. in the name of the so-called protection of the rights of immigrants, you are discriminating against the majority, and in particular in some countries you are making the lives of citizens unbearable in order to impose your ideology. do you not realize how provocative it sounds to the ears of millions of homeless people in greece to call vulnerable groups real or non-minorities, while they are not able to provide even the basics? do you know that it is clearly easier in greece right now to be a refugee or an illegal immigrant than to be an unemployed greek? for example, illegal immigrants have free access to the health system, which is not the case for unemployed greeks. but the people will soon overturn your destructive policy with their vote. now no one doubts the coming historic changes and you fear them. you should be.
the commission mr president, historical experience has shown that economic difficulties, long-term economic recession, but especially the economic crisis and the increase in unemployment among young people, who feel deprived of any prospect of genuine social integration, are decisive factors in the emergence of racism, xenophobia and intolerance. these phenomena seem to be intensifying in the countries of europe where migration flows are increasing, especially the waves of illegal immigrants. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the european union. the fight against poverty therefore involves combating those policies and actions that deepen poverty, provoke war and cause mass displacement. if we do not talk about austerity, the dublin iii regulation, the need for a peace process in the middle east and the need to build societies based on solidarity and mutual aid rather than on inhumane competition, we cannot fight xenophobia and racism.
the commission the obvious inability of political parties and individual politicians to deal with the problems created in all the countries of europe, and especially in greece, by the massive and uncontrolled arrival of millions of illegal immigrants, is pushing them to create new concepts, to distort old ones and to try in this way to say that they will deal with the issue. so the reaction of, for example, parents of children in greece to accept unvaccinated children of illegal immigrants who carry a plethora of diseases into their schools is called racism. the condemnation of the criminal behavior and criminality of illegal immigrants is called xenophobia. when measures are taken against illegal immigrants, then we are extreme and we have bigotry. all of this is designed to create a guilt complex in the world so that it does not react and that is why any reaction is criminalized. but this is the way the world is being divided and racism is being applied against the indigenous people of europe.

in writing. ‒ the the european order for payment is optional, which means that it is available in cross-border cases as an alternative to the various equivalent national procedures. the payment order may be requested by post or, often, by electronic means, does not require the assistance of a lawyer and is enforceable without further formalities in other member states. the existence of two different legal systems for dealing with a single offence would create legal uncertainty and would attempt to deprive the member states' judicial systems of matters falling within their exclusive competence.

on behalf of the ecr group. madam president, after the eurogroup and the troika turned greece into a vast social graveyard by slashing wages and pensions since 2010, after the troika filled the country with armies of unemployed and dismantled labour relations by putting collective agreements in the dustbin of history, now the council is washing its hands like pontius pilate and the european commission is pretending to have become sensitive to the workers in greece. the same applies to the syriza-anel government in the memorandum, which, continuing the memorandum options of new democracy and pasok, is now shedding crocodile tears for the workers, condemning them to starvation wages; a government that is cutting subsidiary pensions, the ecas and selling off public property for a small amount; a government that has not dared to recapitalize the insurance system and to enter german compensation into the state budget; a government that is emancipating the creditors by having a balanced retreat. enough of the hypocrisy and the double-speak! the greek people can no longer tolerate being fooled and will soon send a strong message to the troika and all its subordinates.

in writing. ‒ the the draft commission implementing directive, which aims to amend annexes i to v to directive 2000/29/ec, is contrary to the objectives of regulation (eu) 2016/2031 in that it undermines the requirements for the introduction into the union of certain fruits susceptible to harmful organisms, in particular as regards citrus pollen and citrus cancer. the purpose of regulation (eu) 2016/2031 is to identify the plant health risks posed by each species, strain or biotype of pathogenic agents, animals or parasitic plants harmful to plants or plant products ('pests') and measures to reduce those risks to an acceptable level. the amendment of the implementing directive proposed hereby is therefore considered necessary.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of regulation (eu) 2016/2031 is to identify the plant health risks posed by each species, strain or biotype of pathogenic agents, animals or parasitic plants harmful to plants or plant products ('harmful organisms') and measures to reduce those risks to an acceptable level. i therefore support the amendment of the implementing directive proposed here as necessary.

in writing. ‒ the many children with rare paediatric diseases do not have access to specific paediatric medicines, resulting in unintended medicines being prescribed on the basis of experience without the necessary clinical research. the paediatric regulation has greatly improved drug development and has led to progress in the field of paediatric diseases but there is still a very large margin for improvement. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on paediatric medicines, as it is necessary to ensure that children are given medicines which can effectively and safely treat paediatric diseases.
in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution on paediatric medicines is another attempt to better regulate the framework surrounding the prescription and supply of paediatric medicines, with the aim of protecting children and the population as a whole, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the children are a vulnerable population group and differ from adults in terms of their development, physiology and psychology. research in relation to age and development, and the availability of appropriate pharmaceutical products, are of particular importance. the paediatric medicines regulation was adopted ten years ago to ensure high quality research into the development of medicines for children and the proper authorisation of medicines used by them. the regulation achieved many of its objectives, but several weaknesses were identified in 2013 in the progress report adopted by the commission, in particular as regards paediatric research programmes and paediatric oncology. the commission is therefore urged to adopt urgently any regulatory changes that could help to improve the situation, to strengthen the role of the european paediatric clinical research network and to ensure that member states adopt measures to strengthen research and development and the marketing of paediatric medicines. we therefore support the proposal and vote in favour of it.
